data.name: Moaz
data.gender_notes: Moaz is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic word 'ma'ooz' which means brightness or light. The name Moaz carries the meaning “Brightness, Light” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Moaz usually hope their child will grow to embody brightness, light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the inner light and brightness that guides us through life.
data.etymology: Moaz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brightness, Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Moaz total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_english.name: Moaz
in_english.meaning: Protected by God, safe, in peace
in_english.long_meaning: Moaz is an Islamic name derived from the Arabic root 'عوذ' (awādha), meaning 'to seek protection'. It signifies being under God's protection and safety. Historically, Moaz bin Jabal was a notable companion of Prophet Muhammad, playing a significant role in spreading Islam. The name Moaz is popular among Muslim communities worldwide, symbolizing a parent's prayer for their child's safety and well-being under divine care.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Moaz" holds a significant place in various Islamic cultures across the world. In Sudan, for example, it is a common name for boys and carries a revered status due to renowned historical figures like Sheikh Moaz Bin Jaber, a 14th-century Sudanese poet, scholar, and Sufi teacher. Similarly, in various Arab and Middle Eastern communities, the name is associated with wisdom and knowledge, as evoked by the story of Prophet Moses (Musa in Arabic) who sought knowledge from Allah and became a guiding light for his people.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the name "Moaz" holds a deep significance, as it is a reminder of the inherent light that exists within every individual, as described in the Quran in Surah An-Nur (24:35), "Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His Light is as if there is a niche therein. We drew out a spherical pound of [molten] glass, and we made within it a niche. We were thus cooling it into an elaborate structure. We said, 'Come, Allah, with your forgiveness.' And, 'Come, Allah, with your compassion.' That is Allah, your Lord; exalted is He. [All that remains] is for the faithful to respond [to their Lord]."
